naturalism_issues: Displaying authentic cyanide because a donor demands original contents, despite a conservator objection, feels conspicuously engineered to put poison within reach. Private acquisition status does not make the museum setting more convincing.
An antique poison bottle retaining lethal contents after more than a century requires explanation; its label and receipt do not themselves establish present potency.

The specially requested donor glass, timed camera disconnection, canceled theatrical collapse, and precisely timed safety override cluster as conspicuous plot machinery. Each could be plausible individually.

Documents repeatedly specify interpretive boundaries, such as planned program versus attendance and lighting log versus security log. These read as guidance to puzzle solvers more than ordinary records.
No murder report has yet identified a death, actual poison exposure, or perpetrator action. Motives cannot uniquely solve the case.
